story.title: Joseph
story.subtitle: Dreams, betrayal and purpose

introduction.summary: Joseph moves from a pit to slavery, prison and leadership. Through years of injustice, God develops his character and places him where he can save many lives.
introduction.context: Joseph is one of Jacob’s twelve sons. Family favouritism and jealousy lead to his removal from home, but the story shows God working through circumstances that appear hopeless.

storySections.title: Dreams and Jealousy
storySections.content: Joseph receives dreams suggesting that his family will one day bow before him. His father’s favour and his manner of sharing the dreams deepen his brothers’ jealousy. They sell him to traders and deceive their father into believing Joseph is dead.

storySections.title: Faithful in Egypt
storySections.content: Joseph serves in Potiphar’s household and is entrusted with responsibility. When he refuses an immoral proposal, he is falsely accused and imprisoned. Even there, God remains with him and Joseph continues to serve faithfully.

storySections.title: Forgotten in Prison
storySections.content: Joseph accurately interprets the dreams of two royal officials. He asks the restored cupbearer to remember him, but the cupbearer forgets. Joseph’s release does not come immediately, and the season of waiting continues.

storySections.title: Wisdom Before Pharaoh
storySections.content: When Pharaoh has disturbing dreams, Joseph explains that seven years of abundance will be followed by seven years of famine. He recommends a wise storage plan, and Pharaoh appoints him to lead Egypt’s preparation.

storySections.title: Reconciliation and Purpose
storySections.content: The famine brings Joseph’s brothers to Egypt seeking food. After testing their changed character, Joseph reveals his identity and embraces them. He recognises that although they intended harm, God used the situation to preserve many lives.

keyPeople.name: Joseph
keyPeople.role: Son of Jacob who becomes a leader in Egypt

keyPeople.name: Joseph’s brothers
keyPeople.role: Family members transformed from jealousy toward responsibility

keyPeople.name: Pharaoh
keyPeople.role: Ruler who appoints Joseph over Egypt’s famine preparations

keyLocations.name: Egypt
keyLocations.description: The place of Joseph’s suffering, service and eventual leadership

flashcards.back: Their father showed Joseph special favour, and Joseph shared dreams in which his family bowed before him.

flashcards.front: Where did Joseph’s brothers place him before selling him?
flashcards.back: They threw Joseph into an empty cistern or pit.
He was falsely accused after refusing to betray Potiphar’s trust and sin against God.
Seven years of abundance followed by seven years of severe famine.
Store food during the abundant years so Egypt could survive the famine.

flashcards.front: How did Joseph interpret his brothers’ harmful actions?
flashcards.back: They intended harm, but God used the events to preserve many lives.

keyLessons: Integrity matters even when faithfulness carries a cost.
Delay does not mean God is absent.
Wisdom prepares responsibly for future difficulty.
Forgiveness can break the cycle of revenge.
God can bring redemptive purpose from human wrongdoing without calling the wrongdoing good.

reflection.question: Is there a disappointment or injustice that has tempted you to give up doing what is right?
reflection.prompt: Identify one faithful action you can take even before your circumstances change.

story.prayerPrompt: God who was with Joseph, keep me faithful in difficulty and give me grace to forgive.

quiz.question: What did Joseph’s brothers do to him?
quiz.explanation: The brothers sold Joseph, and he was taken to Egypt.

quiz.question: In whose household did Joseph first serve in Egypt?
quiz.explanation: Potiphar, an Egyptian official, bought Joseph and entrusted his household to him.

quiz.question: How many years of abundance did Pharaoh’s dreams predict?
quiz.explanation: Seven abundant years would be followed by seven years of famine.

quiz.question: Why did Joseph’s brothers travel to Egypt?
options: To buy food during the famine
quiz.explanation: The famine reached Canaan, so Jacob sent his sons to Egypt to buy grain.

quiz.question: How did Joseph eventually treat his brothers?
options: He forgave and provided for them
He refused to speak to them
He sent them away without food
quiz.explanation: Joseph reconciled with his brothers and assured them of his care.
